article.story: Colorado State (3-6) at Washington State (1-8), Nov. 14 at 10:30 p.m. EST. Opening Line: Washington State by 7.5. Against the spread: Washington State 5-4, Colorado State 4-5. How to watch: CBS Sports Network Key stats Washington State Offense Overall: 307.7 yards per game (128th in FBS) Passing: 192.6 yards per game (108th) Rushing: 115.1 yards per game (120th) Scoring: 19 points per game (130th) Washington State Defense Overall: 377.2 yards per game (86th in FBS) Passing: 203 yards per game (53rd) Rushing: 174.2 yards per game (107th) Scoring: 27.4 points per game (95th) Colorado State Offense Overall: 444.1 yards per game (25th in FBS) Passing: 274.8 yards per game (21st) Rushing: 169.3 yards per game (50th) Scoring: 35.8 points per game (20th) Colorado State Defense Overall: 542.2 yards per game (138th in FBS) Passing: 271 yards per game (131st) Rushing: 271.2 yards per game (138th) Scoring: 44.8 points per game (138th) Colorado State ranks 137th in defensive third down percentage, allowing opponents to convert 44.7% of the time. Washington State ranks 118th on offense, converting on 34.1% of third downs. Washington State ranks 132nd in the FBS with a -8 turnover margin, compared to Colorado State's 19th-ranked +6 margin. Washington State is 79th in the FBS averaging 58.2 penalty yards per game, compared to Colorado State's 17th-ranked 42.7 per-game average. Washington State is 105th in FBS in red zone defense, allowing opponents to score on 88.6% of trips. Colorado State's red zone offense ranks 42nd, scoring on 88.6% of red zone opportunities. Colorado State ranks 116th in the FBS with an average time of possession of 28:07. Team leaders Washington State Passing: Caden Pinnick, 952 yards, 3 TDs, 5 INTs, 61.8 completion percentage Rushing: Kirby Vorhees, 292 yards on 66 carries, 4 TDs Receiving: Branden Ganashamoorthy, 459 yards on 34 catches, 3 TDs Colorado State Passing: Hauss Hejny, 1,391 yards, 16 TDs, 2 INTs, 65.4 completion percentage Rushing: Jayden Brown, 456 yards on 54 carries, 3 TDs Receiving: Reginald Vick Jr., 463 yards on 32 catches, 4 TDs Last game Washington State lost 26-20 to San Diego State on Oct. 31. Owen Eshelman threw for 299 yards on 30-of-42 attempts (71.4%) with no touchdowns and one interception. He also carried the ball 16 times for 34 yards and two rushing touchdowns. Vorhees had 17 rushing yards on seven carries and one touchdown, adding three receptions for 16 yards. Daniel Blood put up 105 yards on eight catches. Colorado State fell to Boise State 64-38 on Nov. 7. Hejny threw for 253 yards on 14-of-25 attempts (56.0%) with two touchdowns and no interceptions. He also carried the ball nine times for 69 yards and one rushing touchdown. Damian Moore Jr. carried the ball five times for 50 yards. Tommy Maher recorded 99 yards on six catches with one touchdown. Next game Washington State plays at Texas State on Nov. 21. Colorado State plays at Fresno State on Nov. 21.
